scores.reasoning: The candidate demonstrates consistent creative problem-solving across multiple contexts with specific, measurable outcomes. This maps to Tier 4 (7-8) based on: (1) Multiple concrete examples of innovative solutions with documented impact, (2) Novel approaches that weren't just applying existing methods, (3) Evidence of creative leadership through teaching others. Key innovations include: designing an AI triage-summary system that reduced prep time enough to convert 60-minute appointments to 30-minute slots; creating a single-source mental health guide that solved information architecture problems causing care delays; developing Power Apps/Excel coverage tools and documentation templates. The candidate shows pattern recognition across domains (clinical care, information architecture, AI workflow automation) and translates insights into executable solutions. Not scored 9-10 because innovations are within VA/healthcare context rather than field-redefining contributions.

evidence.quote: I designed a prompt chain that extracts med timeline, diagnoses, allergies, risk flags, monitoring needs, and open tasks into a one-page brief. I ran side-by-side tests with frontline psychiatrists, then iterated with the Chief/Deputy Chief and program managers to set guardrails (human-in-the-loop, audit list, escalation rules). Results: prep time dropped enough to convert overflow new-patient visits to 30 minutes without sacrificing safety checks.
evidence.context: Concrete example of innovative AI solution with specific methodology (prompt chain design, iterative testing, guardrails) and measurable outcome (60-min to 30-min conversion). Shows creative application of AI to clinical workflow problem.

evidence.quote: I mapped available services and identified root causes: naming inconsistencies and missing 'who/when' referral rules. I drafted a single-source MH guide (eligibility, contraindications, how to book), 2 lines per service, and hyperlinked all services to a shared drive with additionally detailed information for mental health providers. We saw fewer misroutes, increase in access to care, and faster routes for urgent cases.
evidence.context: Creative reframing of clinical problem as information architecture challenge. Novel solution (single-source guide with hyperlinks) with documented outcomes (fewer misroutes, increased access).

evidence.quote: The lesson: Information Architecture is clinical care by other means, and good IA reduces waste and risk.
